english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a member of the crew of a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), which was carrying goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), failed to ensure that the vehicle carried such emergency information as required by those regulations

english.notes:
Important: these Regulations have been replaced by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009.

(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be considered subject to current HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
